    The subspace quiver #

    The subspace quiver on an index type ι has a central vertex and one outer vertex for each i : ι, with a single arrow running from each outer vertex into the centre. A representation of it whose arrows act injectively is a family of subspaces of the vector space at the centre, which is where the name comes from.

    Its underlying graph is the star with |ι| leaves. With three leaves this is the Dynkin diagram D₄, and the quiver is the same as LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.D4; with four leaves it is the extended Dynkin diagram D4~, the graph of the classical four subspace problem, and the quiver has infinite representation type (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Subspace.FiniteRepType).

    This file carries the vertex and arrow data alone.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.Subspace: the vertex type, with constructors center and outer, and a Quiver instance whose only arrows are the outer i ⟶ center.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.Subspace.arrow: the arrow from an outer vertex into the centre.

    References #

    • I. M. Gelfand, V. A. Ponomarev, Problems of linear algebra and classification of quadruples of subspaces in a finite-dimensional vector space, Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 5 (1972), 163--237.
    • I. Assem, D. Simson, A. Skowroński, Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras, Volume I, Chapter VII.
